title: TokenX settlement graph
description: Transaction lifecycle from signed intent through inclusion, confirmation, derived indexing, reconciliation, and journal-only recovery. Application reservation owns exclusive product terminals; chain inclusion and confirmation own settlement finality; the indexer owns neither.
assumptions: TokenX is the curriculum's custodial ledger example, not a requirement to run a public chain or wallet product.

Confirmation depth is a named finality threshold (illustrative: wait N subsequent blocks, or the custodial ledger's quorum commit). Deeper confirmation lowers reorg odds; it does not make an indexer authoritative and is not a linearizable application read.
A reorg shallower than the waited depth is an expected chain risk. After a suspected reorg, settlement reads stay UNKNOWN until the chain tip is read again.
Application reservation state (RESERVED then FINALIZED or RELEASED; destination CREDITED or CANCELLED) is a separate authority from chain inclusion and confirmation. Do not collapse them.
Signed request logs are not sufficient evidence for automatic replay. Replay committed chain or journal records only, then fence before new writes.
Indexer rows, cached balances, search, and analytics are derived application state. They own neither exclusive terminals nor settlement finality.

nodes.title: Signed transfer intent
nodes.summary: A signed transfer command is intent, not settlement. Ownership here is not authoritative chain state. The request log proves a client sent a command, not that a ledger or block committed.

detail.consistency: No consistency boundary. Tenant-scoped idempotency key plus request hash identify the command; they do not create chain inclusion or a spendable balance.
detail.durability: The signed request may be archived. That log is not a committed journal and is not replay evidence after restore or reorg.
detail.failure: Timeout, disconnect, or a lost 200 is UNKNOWN, not a failed commit and not confirmed inclusion. Nothing has been included, so a reorg cannot apply yet.
detail.recovery: Retry the same tenant-scoped idempotency key. Do not open a second transfer_id. Do not auto-replay this request-only log. Query reservation and chain state; fence before new writes if restore is in play.

nodes.title: Application reservation (RESERVED)
nodes.summary: Application reservation state owns exclusive product terminals: unique RESERVED insert, then FINALIZED or RELEASED — never both. This is not chain inclusion, not confirmation, and not indexer freshness.

detail.consistency: One atomic unique insert on transfer_id. After RESERVED, a conditional update takes only FINALIZED or RELEASED. Coordinator timeout stays UNRESOLVED until the destination row is known. This boundary is the application ledger, not confirmation depth.
detail.durability: Durable after the application ledger commit (WAL or quorum of the TokenX primary). Chain inclusion is a different authority.
detail.failure: Two RESERVED rows would mint dual spends. Releasing on timeout while the destination later credits mints money. A chain reorg does not rewrite these terminals; do not treat a reorg as permission to fork FINALIZED and RELEASED.
detail.recovery: Insert-if-absent. Stay UNRESOLVED until destination CREDITED or CANCELLED is queried. Replay committed journals only. Request-only outcomes stay UNKNOWN. Fence before new writes. Exclusive terminals remain FINALIZED or RELEASED.

nodes.title: Destination exclusive terminals
nodes.summary: Application destination state owns ABSENT → CREDITED or CANCELLED, never both. Delayed credit after CANCELLED is rejected. This is not chain confirmation and not an indexer row.

detail.consistency: Serializable compare-and-set on transfer_id. CREDITED and CANCELLED are mutually exclusive. CREDITED drives source FINALIZED; CANCELLED drives RELEASED.
detail.durability: The durable destination row is the product terminal. An indexer hit is not this row.
detail.failure: RPC timeout is UNKNOWN, not CANCELLED. A late credit after CANCELLED must lose. Indexer lag must not be treated as ABSENT, and a reorg does not authorize a second terminal.
detail.recovery: Query the committed destination row. Duplicates return the committed outcome. Replay committed journals only. Exclusive terminals remain CREDITED or CANCELLED. Request-only outcomes stay UNKNOWN.

nodes.title: Chain inclusion (this hop succeeded)
nodes.summary: Authoritative chain or ledger inclusion. This hop succeeded in the settlement-succeeds-indexer-fails scenario. Inclusion is settlement authority, not an indexer balance and not a linearizable application read.

detail.consistency: The included record is the chain/ledger fact for this transfer. Application reservation terminals remain a separate authority. Inclusion is not confirmation depth.
detail.durability: Durable as an included transaction or ledger entry. A later reorg can still drop shallow inclusion; confirmation depth is the finality boundary.
detail.failure: Mempool drop, rejection, or a reorg that removes a shallow block. Inclusion failure is not indexer failure. In the named scenario this hop succeeded while the indexer hop failed.
detail.recovery: Re-read chain or ledger state. Do not infer inclusion from a request log or from a stale index. After a suspected reorg, the outcome stays UNKNOWN until the tip is read again.

nodes.title: Confirmation depth (this hop succeeded)
nodes.summary: Confirmation depth is the finality boundary. This hop succeeded in the settlement-succeeds-indexer-fails scenario. A confirmation is not a linearizable application read and is not preserved under reorg. Deeper confirmation lowers reorg odds; it does not make an indexer authoritative.

detail.consistency: Waiting the named depth reduces reorg probability. It does not provide linearizable application reads, does not replace exclusive terminals, and does not license spendable reads from the indexer.
detail.durability: Finality is probabilistic on a reorgable chain until the named depth. TokenX as a custodial ledger example may treat quorum commit as inclusion-equivalent; that still is not indexer authority.
detail.failure: A reorg deeper than the waited confirmations invalidates the prior confirmation. That is a chain-tip change, not indexer lag. In the named scenario confirmation still stands while the indexer hop failed.
detail.recovery: Wait the named depth again after reorg. Reconciliation stays UNKNOWN until the chain tip is read again. Do not treat surviving index rows as confirmation.

nodes.title: Indexer (this hop failed)
nodes.summary: Derived balances, search, and history projections. This hop failed in the settlement-succeeds-indexer-fails scenario. A lagging or dead indexer is not spendable authority. Chain inclusion and confirmation still succeeded.

detail.consistency: At-least-once ingest with an eventual projection. Never read-your-writes for spendable balances. Not a consistency boundary for money.
detail.durability: Rebuildable from committed chain or journal records. Indexer disks are not the ledger.
detail.failure: This hop failed: ingest stall, crash, or corrupt projection while inclusion and confirmation still succeeded. Serving spendable reads from this index would treat stale derived state as settlement. A reorg is diagnosed from the chain tip, not from this projection.
detail.recovery: Do not serve spendable reads from the index. Replay committed chain or journal records only. Do not auto-replay a request-only log. Fence before new writes. Reconciliation stays UNKNOWN until the chain tip is read again.

nodes.title: Cached balances
nodes.summary: Derived cached balances. Not spendable authority. When the indexer hop has failed, this healthy-path cache is not currently trustworthy.

detail.consistency: TTL or explicit invalidation. A cache hit is not TokenX available balance and is not chain confirmation.
detail.durability: Rebuildable. Flush is not money loss.
detail.failure: After the indexer hop fails, this cache can still look healthy while serving stale derived balances. Reorg and UNKNOWN reservation are invisible here.
detail.recovery: Fail closed on spendable reads. Rebuild from chain or ledger after the tip is read again. Do not promote cache to authority. Do not auto-replay a request-only log.

nodes.title: Analytics and search
nodes.summary: Derived analytics and search. Not settlement. When the indexer hop has failed, this healthy-path view is not currently trustworthy.

detail.consistency: Near-real-time at best. Dashboards may be labeled stale; they still must not authorize spends.
detail.failure: Lag, corrupt mapping, or continuing to look healthy while the indexer feed is dead. A reorg will not be visible here until the chain tip is re-read.
detail.recovery: Drop and rebuild from committed chain or journal records only. Request-only outcomes stay UNKNOWN.

nodes.title: Indexer versus chain tip
nodes.summary: Compares derived index rows to the authoritative chain tip. Mismatch stays UNKNOWN until chain state is read again. Indexer failure does not unwind inclusion or confirmation.

detail.consistency: The chain tip is the settlement read. The index is a suspect. A mismatch is UNKNOWN, not CANCELLED and not a new exclusive terminal.
detail.durability: Reconciliation writes no new money. It records UNKNOWN until a fresh chain read.
detail.failure: If the indexer hop failed, this job cannot prove the derived view; it also must not invent a reorg. Timeout reading the tip keeps UNKNOWN. Serving the last good index as a spendable read is the invalidating mistake.
detail.recovery: Read the chain tip again. Do not auto-replay a request-only log to close the gap. Fence before new writes if repair requires restore. Exclusive terminals remain CREDITED/CANCELLED and FINALIZED/RELEASED.

nodes.title: Journal-only recovery
nodes.summary: Replay committed chain or journal records only. Request-only outcomes stay UNKNOWN. Fence before new writes. Exclusive terminals remain CREDITED or CANCELLED and FINALIZED or RELEASED.

detail.consistency: Recovery must not fork exclusive terminals. A replayed journal row returns the committed outcome; it does not create a second transfer_id. Chain finality is still read from inclusion and confirmation, not from this procedure.
detail.durability: Committed journals (included chain records, WAL, outbox rows that committed with the ledger) are the only automatic replay source.
detail.failure: Auto-replaying request logs can mint a transfer that never included or double-apply one that did. Reorg after shallow confirmation stays UNKNOWN until the tip is re-read. Indexer failure is not a license to mint from HTTP archives.
detail.recovery: Replay committed chain or journal records only. Fence the writer epoch before new writes. Keep CREDITED/CANCELLED and FINALIZED/RELEASED exclusive. Query UNKNOWN by transfer_id.

nodes.title: Request-only log (not replay evidence)
nodes.summary: Proves a client sent a command. Not inclusion, not confirmation, not an indexer rebuild source. Request-only outcomes stay UNKNOWN.

detail.consistency: No settlement consistency. Presence in this log does not imply RESERVED, CREDITED, or chain inclusion.
detail.durability: May outlive the process. Still not a committed journal.
detail.failure: Treating this log as missing-and-must-mint after indexer failure, reorg, or restore invents transfers. A signed request is not proof the original commit happened.
detail.recovery: Leave UNKNOWN. Query reservation, destination terminals, and chain tip by transfer_id. Do not auto-replay. Fence before new writes.

edges.label: Reserve with idempotency key; not chain inclusion
Submit / broadcast; settlement starts at inclusion

scenarios.title: Settlement succeeds, indexer fails
scenarios.summary: Chain inclusion and confirmation still succeeded. The indexer hop failed. Derived balances are stale and are not spendable authority.
scenarios.callout: Chain settlement stands; derived balances are stale; do not serve spendable reads from the index; reconciliation stays UNKNOWN until the chain tip is read again; do not auto-replay a request-only log; fence before new writes.
